title: Rajkummar Rao Hints at 'Pressure' Behind Modi Song Appearance, Deletes Comment
excerpt: The actor's now-deleted Instagram reply admitting to pressure over the 'Modi Hai Toh Mumkin Hai' music video has gone viral amid student protests across India.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Rajkummar Rao's deleted comment hints at pressure to appear in a pro-BJP music video.
  • His admission sparked debate about coercion in Bollywood's political involvement.
  • Rao previously expressed support for student protests demanding education reforms.
  • Other Bollywood stars, including Salman Khan and Alia Bhatt, have backed the protests.

Rajkummar Rao found himself at the centre of a social media firestorm on Wednesday after a now-deleted Instagram comment appeared to acknowledge that he had faced pressure to appear in the pro-BJP music video "Modi Hai Toh Mumkin Hai." The admission, brief as it was, has reignited questions about the relationship between Bollywood and political power.

The chain of events began when the 41-year-old actor posted a statement on Instagram expressing solidarity with students protesting at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The demonstrations, organized under the CJP banner, centre on allegations of NEET paper leaks and demands for sweeping education reforms, including the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

The Deleted Reply

While many praised Rao's post, a section of users reminded him that he was among several actors — alongside Varun Dhawan, Vikrant Massey, and Arshad Warsi — who featured in the "Modi Hai Toh Mumkin Hai" music video released last year. The track, composed by Meet Bros with vocals by Adarsh Shukla and Divya Bhatt, was widely viewed as a promotional effort for Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

An Instagram user named @om.ar510 wrote: "I had huge respect for you man... you lost it with one propaganda song!!! I never miss any of your movies, never thought you would sold off so easily."

Rao responded directly, and the full text of his reply was captured in screenshots before he removed it.

"I can never sell my soul, brother. And one song does not define who I am, what I stand for, or what my ideologies in life are. You can never know the pressure."

— Rajkummar Rao, in a now-deleted Instagram comment

He added: "I stand for what is right and what keeps us united as human beings. As long as my conscience is clean and I work the hardest nothing else matters. People who know me personally know who I am and hopefully, one day, I'll be able to earn back your respect."

Online Reaction and Debate

The word "pressure" became the focal point of the debate. Some users took the comment as a direct admission that Bollywood actors are coerced into participating in political content. "Rajkummar Rao admitted being pressurised into the Modi song. This is huge. Citizens have awakened the conscience of spineless actors now and this is just the beginning of true change," one widely shared post on X read.

Others pushed back. "Pressure? What kind of pressure on you man? You are a successful artist and youth follows every reaction of you," one commenter wrote. Another simply noted: "He accepted… They are under pressure to sing such songs."

Bollywood's Political Landscape
›Rajkummar Rao faced backlash for 'Modi Hai Toh Mumkin Hai' video.
›Rao's comment about 'pressure' ignited discussions on coercion in Bollywood.
›Support for student protests from Bollywood figures is growing.
›Critics labeled Rao's protest statement as 'vanilla' and ineffective.

The deletion of the comment only amplified scrutiny, with screenshots continuing to circulate across X and Instagram long after the original was removed.

A Broader Pattern

Rao's initial statement on the protests had itself drawn mixed reactions. While it expressed support for students, critics called it "vanilla" and accused him of "using so many words for saying nothing." The post read in part: "When young people feel unheard, it is a reminder that society must listen. Every voice deserves to be heard with dignity, fairness and respect."

He is far from the only Bollywood figure navigating the tension between personal views and political alignment. On Wednesday night, Salman Khan posted a statement saying "my heart goes out to the students and their families who were hurt." On Thursday morning, R Madhavan and Alia Bhatt followed with their own messages of support. Actors Huma Qureshi, Shabana Azmi, and Prakash Raj have participated directly in protests, while comedian Abish Mathew and actor Ayesha Khan were briefly detained by Mumbai police for joining a CJP demonstration.

What to Watch

The episode underscores an uncomfortable reality for the Indian film industry: as public sentiment shifts, the political postures that once carried little cost are now met with sharp accountability from audiences. Whether Rao's deleted comment leads other actors to address their own participation in similar political projects remains to be seen. On the work front, the actor is next set to play former cricketer Sourav Ganguly in a biopic, according to Telegraph India.
